newsitem.title: UK: UK business confidence at record high -CIMA survey.
newsitem.headline: UK business confidence at record high -CIMA survey.

text.p: Over three quarters of directors in Britain's manufacturing, service and public sectors are "fairly or very optimistic" about the outlook for their businesses in the next 12 months, the Chartered Institute of Management Accountants said on Wednesday.
The CIMA said in a summary of its latest quarterly survey that two in three financial controllers and directors were optimistic about Britain's economic prospects as a whole.
The CIMA said both findings were records. It said it began conducting the business surveys among its senior members in 1993.
But the survey showed that employers were increasingly concerned about rising wages, with over half of those questioned saying wages were growing at a faster pace than average costs, the CIMA said.
The CIMA said half the organisations questioned expected to take on more people in the coming year, with only 14 percent expected to shed jobs.

It said 62 percent of finance directors now believed Britain would join the single European currency in the next five years, compared with 42 percent in the last survey in November 1996. But only 24 percent of businesses said they were making plans for the transition to a single currency.
